title: 6Sense Filter
subtitle: Six-dimensional qualification screening that converts the costly question "should we invest?" into a structured, evidence-based answer — before equity is committed.

sections.heading: The Six-Dimensional Architecture
sections.body:
The 6Sense Filter evaluates every venture across six operational dimensions. A company must pass all six — the filter exists to say no early and cheaply, not to manufacture reasons to proceed.

① DIRECTION
Is the problem real, the market sizeable, and the founder thesis credible? Verified by actual buying behaviour and search intent data — not broad market size estimates.

② ENERGY
Does the business model generate substantially more value from each customer than it costs to acquire them? Cash flow sustainability and the time it takes to recover acquisition costs are tracked alongside long-term customer value.

③ CAPACITY
Does the team and infrastructure have the operational capability to execute at scale? Equipment utilisation, working capital efficiency, and supply chain constraints must all be mapped before growth capital is allocated.

④ PRIORITISATION
Is the roadmap sequenced for capital efficiency, not feature maximalism? Data quality >= 3 stars on AI Compass. Business model structurally generates the data it needs — designed data gaps are permanent.

⑤ RISK
Does the risk model account for regulatory exposure, not just commercial risk? Platform dependency, decision-making blind spots, and worst-case scenarios must all be assessed — not just upside projections.

⑥ DECISION
Does the leadership team have the governance capability to make structured decisions under uncertainty? Decision holds absolute veto power. A company that cannot make structured decisions under uncertainty will fail regardless of the other five dimensions.

sections.heading: Turning Regulatory Complexity into Competitive Advantage
sections.body:
Traditional venture qualification frameworks fail in high-barrier industries because they treat compliance as cost. The 6Sense Filter embeds regulatory architecture, cybersecurity posture, and data governance directly into early-stage evaluation — because in regulated markets, these are not overhead. They are the moat.

A company that clears the 6Sense Filter in a regulated domain has already begun building the barriers that keep competitors out. Regulation is not a burden — it is the moat, if you structure for it early.

The filter also embeds adoption realism: addressable market claims are discounted by diffusion position. A product that requires late-majority adoption to hit plan fails the Direction dimension regardless of its headline TAM.

sections.heading: Information Asymmetry as the Core Problem
sections.body:
Early-stage markets are lemon markets. Founders make claims; investors cannot easily verify them. The 6Sense process is, economically, an information-asymmetry reduction engine — each dimension converts founder claims into verifiable evidence before equity is committed.

The filter distinguishes between two categories of data: data that the business model structurally generates, and data that improved tooling could collect. Designed data gaps are permanent architectural decisions. They cannot be fixed after the fact. The 6Sense process surfaces this distinction before capital is at risk.
